text:
Question for anyone who has thought about citing metrics sites, or any data that updates daily. Someone wants to cite their package's page on the R Observatory, which I run, in a dissertation (<https://github.com/r-observatory/feedback/issues/1|https://github.com/r-observatory/feedback/issues/1>). My instinct is to send them to citation("pkg") and the CRAN package DOI instead.

When is a resource like this worth citing at all, and is the right object the page, the dated data release being used in the viewer, or the project as a whole? And is a Zenodo DOI or a JSS / JOSS / R Journal paper worth pursuing for it?

text:
I am very much in agreement with you on sending them to the CRAN DOI instead if it is a package.  Some folks (CRAN, R Foundation, ...) have done quite some work to get packages their own DOIs (and also pay a few pennies for each package to make this possible); so this should be used and promoted, and `citation("pkg")` does that.

Whether an aggregation as you provide in the R Observatory is "also" (or "equally" or even "preferably") citeable may be an open question.  Yours is (as usual) a very impressive project; it is also still very young. Maybe time will tell if it becomes eminently citeable, and cited.  In the interim, you can of course pursue the path of a publication for the novel work you did there (and getting a Zenodo DOI may be the quickest path to something identifiable).
